Repo: /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph (Turborepo; Next.js site in apps/website, Supabase in packages/database). Work on branch `main` in the main checkout; read only, change nothing.

I need a grounded picture of what EXISTS TODAY for auth/access-control, so I can estimate how much work each of several proposed agent-access designs would be. Investigate and report with file paths and exact identifiers:

1. Supabase schema & access control in packages/database: the tables that model access (look for Space / SpaceAccess / Group / group_membership / ResourceAccess / Concept / Content / account tables), and the RLS policies on them. Find `my_user_accounts()` and any related SECURITY DEFINER functions — how many there are, what they do.
2. `upsert_account_in_space` — what it does and whether it grants access as a side effect.
3. How a Space authenticates today: is the website login a Supabase session for a "space account"? Where are the space credentials created/stored (look in apps/website auth routes, and in apps/roam / apps/obsidian for how the plugin logs in to Supabase)?
4. Supabase edge functions: list them (supabase/functions/*), especially `create-space`, `create-group`, and anything named like `create-agent`. Note whether they use the service/secret key and whether they check the caller's role.
5. Any existing MCP server, headless API route, or token-handoff code already in the repo (search for "mcp", "handoff", "agent", "token" under apps/website/app/api, apps/roam, apps/obsidian, packages/*). Is there an existing /auth/ route for plugin→website handoff?
6. Whether there is any existing `agent_reader` role, `agent_grant` table, or access-token hook.

Report concisely but concretely — what exists, what doesn't, and roughly how large each relevant area is (file counts / line counts). This is for effort estimation, so flag anything that looks like it would be a big lift to change.

- aiday: Daily interactive check-in for Trang's AI engineering curriculum. Runs the morning kickoff — free recall of yesterday, adversarial grilling on the gaps, then a learning note written to the Obsidian vault — before setting today's focus. Also handles mid-build unblocking that stays in scope, and tracks progress numbers. Use when the user runs /aiday, says they're starting or resuming a curriculum day, wants to recall or be quizzed on what they learned, wants to write up a day's learning notes, or says they're stuck while working through it.
- babysit: Keep a PR merge-ready by triaging comments, resolving clear conflicts, and fixing CI in a loop.
- checkpoint: Record or update the session context for the current worktree into the Obsidian vault so a future session (or the user) can resume with full reasoning-layer context. Use when the user asks to checkpoint, save session context, snapshot progress, or when wrapping up meaningful work on a ticket.
- create-pr: Get a branch reviewer-ready and open a ready-for-review PR: load the approved plan, audit comments, run ci:validate and bot-thread checks, run the delegated review and scope-check, check drift against the plan, and fill the repo PR template with a reviewer diagram and verification evidence. Opens the PR only when the plan says ship_when_verified: yes. Pass --dry-run to print the body without pushing.
- dg-delegated-full-review: Run a comprehensive, read-only code review in a separate subagent, return the findings to the primary agent, and close or archive the review task when supported. Use only when explicitly invoked for a pull request, branch, commit, diff, or current changes.
- dg-engineering-writing-style: Draft and revise engineering emails, chat messages, requests, follow-ups, status updates, engineering tickets, PR comments, issue reports, release notes, technical documentation, and other team writing in the shared Discourse Graphs style. Use whenever a Discourse Graphs engineer asks to write, rewrite, phrase, shorten, clarify, or polish team communication or documentation, unless they request a different style.

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Agent-created Engineering tickets

For all agent-created Engineering tickets, including direct Linear tool calls and tickets created through other skills, use [dg-create-engineering-ticket](.agents/skills/dg-create-engineering-ticket/SKILL.md). Create them in `Ticket Draft` with exactly one workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group: `Created by Claude`, `Created by Codex`, or `Created by LLM` for another or unknown agent. Record the creation skills actually used in `Notes`, and verify those fields after creation. If no skill was used, record `Created with: direct agent workflow (no skill)` and still apply the same review rules.

The requesting human reviews intent, scope, acceptance criteria, and ticket-writing standards before approving a move to `Triage` or `Backlog`. Keep the provenance label after approval. See the skill for transitions and missing-configuration handling. This applies to new tickets; do not retrospectively classify existing tickets.

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues. For PRs over 400 changed lines, excluding tests, include a concise split justification, main review entry points, and testing path in Reviewer brief.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Required standards

- Read and follow [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md) and the nested `AGENTS.md` files that apply to changed files before editing or reviewing code.
- Follow [PR_GUIDELINES.md](PR_GUIDELINES.md) for scope, verification, and review requirements. General code standards live in the style guide; app-specific instructions remain in nested `AGENTS.md` files.
- Before handoff or requesting review, run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` from `.agents/skills/dg-pr-adherence-check/SKILL.md` against the final diff and available PR metadata. Resolve findings or report them explicitly, including missing evidence. Rerun affected checks after changes.

# UI constraints

Always-on constraints for any UI edit in this monorepo. The Figma workflow, the token
values, and the per-app reference tables moved to the `figma-implementation` skill; invoke
it when implementing a design.

- **Check `packages/ui/src/components/ui/` before writing a new shared component.** Button,
  Card, Label, Checkbox, Select, Textarea and Badge already exist.
- **No hardcoded hex colors in shared components.** Use the Tailwind theme tokens from
  `packages/tailwind-config` or the CSS variables in `packages/ui/src/globals.css`.
- **The three apps do not share a UI stack.** `apps/website` uses `@repo/ui`; `apps/roam`
  uses BlueprintJS and deliberately does not use `@repo/ui`; `apps/obsidian` uses custom
  React with Tailwind mapped to Obsidian CSS variables.

TypeScript, naming, and general UI conventions live in `STYLE_GUIDE.md`.
